definition: Objective-relative resource shortfall over a declared horizon.
uncertainty: income variance, hidden commitments, acquisition-rate error
validation: predict whether desired conversion can complete by deadline

definition: Marginal strategic value of one additional resource unit at a declared horizon.
formula: marginal improvement in best feasible objective outcome

definition: Expected time until a capability can produce its intended effect.
validation: compare predicted readiness with observed effect time

definition: Probability that a capability accomplishes its objective under current conditions.
uncertainty: hidden enemy state and model error

definition: Duration for which current capability can be maintained before a limiting resource/production condition is reached.
Elapsed time from strategic demand to usable capability.
Limiting factor preventing desired capability growth at required rate.
validation: remove/relax one constraint and measure capability response

definition: Interval in which expected action value exceeds a declared baseline by a material margin.
validation: hit/miss rate plus post-window value decay

definition: Degree to which an actor constrains opponent decisions while retaining meaningful alternatives.
validation: measure action-set restriction and response burden

definition: Weighted value of materially feasible future transitions remaining after a decision.
validation: compare option-set changes against later recovery flexibility

definition: Objective progress achieved per unit of total strategic commitment cost.
Strategic cost imposed on an opponent by an action, relative to the opponent's prior feasible transition set.
formula: change in opponent feasible transition value
validation: compare expected enemy transition with post-response feasible set

definition: Expected improvement in best decision from additional information minus acquisition cost.
formula: E[value(best action after information)] - E[value(best action now)] - acquisition_cost
validation: compare information-gathering choices against no-information baseline

definition: Value lost by selecting an action rather than the best feasible alternative using only information available then.
Degree to which an outcome discriminates between competing causal hypotheses.
Acceptable performance retained across plausible perturbations of hidden or uncertain state.
Cost required to exit or redirect a commitment after initiation.
validation: measure recovery cost after commitment interruption

definition: Expected degradation in belief reliability as supporting evidence ages or state changes.
formula: confidence degradation conditional on evidence age and state volatility

definition: Strength of evidence that an action materially caused an observed outcome rather than merely preceded it.
Finite capacity to coordinate simultaneous strategic commitments and information tasks.
